function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are some great ways to order a cake, depending on what you’re looking for:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips |
|--------|----------------|--------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; you can see the shop and talk to the baker. | Call or visit the bakery’s website. Many have online ordering forms or accept orders via email. | Ask about flavors, sizes, and delivery times. Some bakeries offer same‑day pickup or delivery. |
| **Specialty cake shops** | Gourmet, themed, or dietary‑specific cakes (gluten‑free, vegan, keto). | Browse their online catalog, pick a design, and place an order through their website. | Check the “custom” section if you want a personalized message or design. |
| **Online grocery delivery (Instacart, Amazon Fresh, Walmart Grocery)** | You can order a pre‑made cake from a grocery store and have it delivered to your door. | Add the cake to your cart and choose a delivery slot. | Delivery windows may vary; confirm the time window before checkout. |
| **Food‑delivery apps (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates)** | Many restaurants and bakeries partner with these apps. | Search “cake” or “bakery” in the app, pick a shop, and place your order. | Look for “special instructions” to add a message or delivery note. |
| **Online cake retailers (Goldbelly, Cake Delivery, Bakeology)** | Nationwide delivery of specialty cakes (e.g., wedding cakes, novelty cakes). | Choose a cake, customize it, and pay online. | Shipping times can be longer; order at least a week in advance for big events. |
| **DIY kits (Amazon, Walmart, local craft stores)** | All the ingredients and instructions to bake a cake at home. | Buy a kit online or in-store. | Great for a fun activity or if you want full control over flavors. |

### Quick Steps to Order a Cake Online

1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.).  
2. **Choose a style** (classic vanilla, chocolate, fruit, vegan, gluten‑free, etc.).  
3. **Pick a size** (number of servings or dimensions).  
4. **Add a custom message** if you want a personalized touch.  
5. **Select delivery or pickup** and confirm the date/time.  
6. **Pay securely** (most sites accept credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, etc.).  
7. **Confirm the order** via email or the app, and keep the receipt.

### If You’re in a Specific City

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated bakeries and delivery services in your area. Just drop the location, and I’ll give you a tailored recommendation!
